import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import xgboost as xgb
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
import os
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Paths
INPUT_DIR = "./input"
SUBMISSION_DIR = "./submission"
train_path = f"{INPUT_DIR}/train.csv"
test_path = f"{INPUT_DIR}/test.csv"
sample_submission_path = f"{INPUT_DIR}/sample_submission.csv"
submission_path = f"{SUBMISSION_DIR}/submission.csv"

# Create submission directory if it doesn't exist
os.makedirs(SUBMISSION_DIR, exist_ok=True)

print(f"Loading data from {train_path} and {test_path}...")
train_df = pd.read_csv(train_path)
test_df = pd.read_csv(test_path)
sample_submission = pd.read_csv(sample_submission_path)

print(f"Train shape: {train_df.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test_df.shape}")

# Identify columns
target_col = "target"
id_col = "id"
feature_cols = [c for c in train_df.columns if c not in [id_col, target_col]]

# Extract id columns separately before any transformations
train_ids = train_df[id_col].values
test_ids = test_df[id_col].values

# Handle the high cardinality categorical feature 'f_27' using target mean encoding
f_27_col = "f_27"
y_train = train_df[target_col].values
X_train = train_df[feature_cols].copy()
X_test = test_df[feature_cols].copy()

# Calculate target mean for each category in f_27 (Training set only)
f_27_counts = X_train[f_27_col].value_counts()
f_27_target_means = train_df.groupby(f_27_col)[target_col].mean().to_dict()
f_27_global_mean = y_train.mean()

# Encode f_27 in training and test data
encoded_train_f27 = X_train[f_27_col].map(f_27_target_means).fillna(f_27_global_mean)
encoded_test_f27 = X_test[f_27_col].map(f_27_target_means).fillna(f_27_global_mean)

X_train[f_27_col] = encoded_train_f27
X_test[f_27_col] = encoded_test_f27

# Prepare final feature matrix (id column is kept separately)
X_train_final = X_train.copy()
X_test_final = X_test.copy()
y_train_final = y_train

# Split training data into train and validation (hold-out)
X_tr, X_val, y_tr, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train_final, y_train_final, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_train_final
)

# Scale features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_tr_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_tr)
X_val_scaled = scaler.transform(X_val)
X_train_final_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train_final)
X_test_final_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test_final)

print("Training XGBoost model on training split...")
model = xgb.XGBClassifier(
    objective="binary:logistic",
    eval_metric="auc",
    tree_method="hist",
    use_label_encoder=False,
    verbosity=0,
    n_estimators=300,
    max_depth=5,
    learning_rate=0.05,
    subsample=0.8,
    colsample_bytree=0.8,
    random_state=42,
)
model.fit(X_tr_scaled, y_tr)

print("Calculating AUC-ROC on validation set...")
y_val_pred = model.predict_proba(X_val_scaled)[:, 1]
val_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, y_val_pred)
print(f"Validation AUC-ROC Score: {val_auc:.4f}")

# Train on full training data for final submission
print("Training final model on full training data...")
model_final = xgb.XGBClassifier(
    objective="binary:logistic",
    eval_metric="auc",
    tree_method="hist",
    use_label_encoder=False,
    verbosity=0,
    n_estimators=300,
    max_depth=5,
    learning_rate=0.05,
    subsample=0.8,
    colsample_bytree=0.8,
    random_state=42,
)
model_final.fit(X_train_final_scaled, y_train_final)

print("Generating predictions on test set...")
test_probs = model_final.predict_proba(X_test_final_scaled)[:, 1]

# Create submission dataframe using preserved test_ids
submission_df = pd.DataFrame({id_col: test_ids, "target": test_probs})

# Save submission
submission_df.to_csv(submission_path, index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to {submission_path}")
print(f"Submission shape: {submission_df.shape}")
plan: The bug stems from `X_test` never containing the `id` column because it was excluded from `feature_cols` when initially created, and subsequent processing only operated on the feature subset. Additionally, the code attempts to access `X_test[id_col]` after feature modifications without preserving the identifier. The fix requires extracting and preserving the `id` column separately from the feature matrix throughout all transformations, then using it to construct the submission dataframe with predictions on the full test set.
